title: A deactivated person whose toggle is on reads technician false
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Have a valid Public API key for the test organization, the Public API documentation for staff, and a request tool (Postman or any tool that sends requests with that key).
  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have a new staff member for this test, staff member A, on the built-in Technician role, with Time Clock on and Technician on, enrolled at the test location only, then deactivated with Deactivate Account.
  • Note staff member A's id as the Public API gives it (from GET /api/v1/staff).
custom_steps:
1. Send GET /api/v1/staff/<staff member A's id> with the API key.
  2. Reactivate staff member A on the Deactivated tab of Settings, Staff.
  3. Send GET /api/v1/staff/<staff member A's id> with the API key.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The request succeeds.
  • The record includes "technician": false, although the toggle is on.

Step 2:

  • Staff member A is active again.

Step 3:

  • The record now includes "technician": true.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Technician Toggle", Confluence 977371146, version 17 (2 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 2 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11788, story SV-11879 (Story 1, Technician toggle on a staff member), story SV-11883 (Story 5, Public API - technician value on staff)

  • S5-E1: “The value is the result of S5-R1, not the toggle alone: a deactivated person whose toggle is on reads false.”
  • S5-R1: “Each staff record the Public API returns includes a read-only technician value: true when the person is active, their Technician toggle is on and their Time Clock is on (the same rule as the staff list column, S4-R1), otherwise false. A deactivated person is always false.”
  • S1-E2: “A deactivated staff member keeps their Technician toggle as it was, but is not a technician while deactivated (Story 3). Reactivating them brings it back as it was.”
